text.title: Stocks surge to close best week since 2022 as tech rebounds from AI jitters; VIX falls 11%
text.summary: US stocks rallied in a holiday-shortened session. The Nasdaq rose 2.3%, the S&P 500 1.6%, the Russell 2000 1.7% and the Dow 1.2%, which capped the Dow's best week since 2022 and the Nasdaq's best since April. The VIX fell 11.2% to 23.81 and is down 33.7% over five days, so demand for downside protection eased. Cross-asset signals were mixed: the 10-year yield rose 8 bp to 4.93%, the dollar index gained 0.4%, oil slipped 0.8% and gold jumped 2.9%. The main thread is a relief bounce in AI-linked shares after a brutal month, with volatility compressing, though the S&P 500 is still 5.8% below its one-month high.
text.rates: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 8 bp to 4.93%, though it is still 22 bp below its one-month high and 12 bp lower over five days. The 2-year was 4.61% as of Wednesday's Treasury close. Higher yields raise the discount rate on future earnings, which usually weighs on richly valued growth stocks, so tech's gain came despite that headwind. The dollar index rose 0.4% to 104.05. WTI fell 0.8% to $82.99 and is down 19.3% over a month, while Iraq is reported to be seeking a higher OPEC quota ahead of an OPEC+ meeting. Gold's 2.9% jump alongside a firmer dollar and higher yields is unusual, and the headlines do not explain it.
text.breadth: Leadership was cyclical and growth-oriented. Technology rose 2.8%, discretionary 2.1%, communication services 2.0%, materials 1.8% and industrials 1.6%. Defensives lagged: health care and utilities each rose 0.3%, staples 0.4% and real estate 0.6%. Small caps kept pace, with the Russell 2000 up 1.7%, four straight gains and a 3.6% five-day rise. J.P. Morgan's weekly recap (as of Nov 20) showed growth far behind value year to date, so today's tilt toward growth reads as a bounce from oversold levels rather than a settled shift. Abroad, the FTSE 100 posted its biggest weekly gain in eight months on miners and banks.
text.context: The S&P 500 is up 1.7% over five days but still down 5.8% over one month, and the Nasdaq is 9.1% below its one-month high. The Dow and Russell 2000 have each risen four straight sessions. J.P. Morgan's recap noted the S&P 500 traded at 16.4x forward earnings as of Nov 20, after the prior week's sharp sell-off, and today's rally recovers part of that drop.
text.takeaway: Sharp rebounds after steep drawdowns are a normal feature of volatile markets, and one strong week does not settle the trend. For diversified long-term investors, the episode shows how concentrated recent swings have been in AI-linked areas.
text.talk: Stocks bounced hard this week, led by tech after a rough November, and the VIX fell sharply. The market is still below its recent highs, and AI-related volatility has not gone away.

drivers.t: Technology was the top sector, up 2.8%, followed by consumer discretionary at 2.1% and communication services at 2.0%. WSJ reports tech jumped as investors took a break from AI jitters, and the Nasdaq finished its best week since April. Long-duration growth stocks tend to rebound hardest when volatility fades and money returns to beaten-down areas. The FT notes the AI trade has been eclipsed by wild swings in a market struggling to price future earnings. That suggests today's move is as much about positioning as about new fundamentals.

Bloomberg says the message from Washington this week was that the US must win the AI race with China and that the government is prepared to intervene. Policy support can lift sentiment toward AI-exposed companies, but it also adds uncertainty about what intervention would look like. That helps explain why this week was described as wild even as indexes ended higher. Headlines do not specify which policies drove today's session.

drivers.h: Nvidia bounces but stays deep red
drivers.t: Nvidia rose sharply this week with Jensen Huang's return, yet it is still down nearly 28% for November and 21% for 2026. CNBC describes the rally sparked by his return as fleeting, with AI jitters persisting. A bounce from depressed levels in the market's largest AI bellwether helps lift index-level sentiment. The scale of the November drawdown shows how much of the market's recent damage was concentrated in this theme.

drivers.h: AI listings and deals stay in focus
drivers.t: Anthropic shares climbed above their $83 IPO price after a volatile first week on the Nasdaq. SpaceX rose over 4% amid the tech rally, after Elon Musk said he would donate shares to American children every year. These moves suggest risk appetite for AI and tech-adjacent names recovered alongside the broader tech bounce. Newly public shares trade on sentiment, so they can amplify swings in either direction.

Bloomberg projects Black Friday spending to rise, with wary shoppers hunting deals and retail sales expected to top $1 trillion for the first time. Consumer discretionary rose 2.1%, consistent with that tone. Meanwhile the US goods trade deficit widened as AI-related imports hit a record, and the president has demanded a probe of a large upward GDP revision. Strong demand data can lift the growth outlook, but it can also keep yields elevated.

watch.why: Both report after the close Monday and may show whether tech and software sentiment is holding up after the rebound.
Iraq is seeking a higher quota ahead of it, and oil, already down about 19% in a month, is sensitive to supply decisions.
Bloomberg expects a first slowdown in five months, and it bears on European rate expectations and the dollar.
